blocks.why: Normal night at home so I start the month rested — tomorrow is a 20:30 local report and an all-night crossing to Bogota.
Siesta before the BOG night flight; I'll be awake until 08:35 body time, so I want three hours in the bank before I leave the door at 16:55Z.
Straight to bed at the hotel at 02:30 Bogota time after a ten-hour sector — sleep now while I'm still tired enough not to care what the clock says.
A proper Bogota night, 23:00 to 07:00 local, to load up before tonight's 12-hour duty back to Madrid.
Early-afternoon top-up in BOG before a 22:10Z report — this nap is what gets me through the second half of the flight.
Home by 11:50Z off a night crossing; three hours to take the edge off, then I get up so I can still sleep tonight.
Deliberately early to bed — standby opens at 04:00Z tomorrow, which is 06:00 local, so this is the only sleep I'll get before it.
Full night back on Madrid time; tomorrow's standby doesn't start until midday so I can sleep normally.
Eight hours before the Boston trip — report is 06:55Z so I'm out the door at 05:20Z and I want that sleep finished, not interrupted.
Curtains shut at 13:15 Boston time — it's 19:15 on my body clock, so this counts as the night's sleep before the 01:50Z red-eye home.
Just landed off a duty that ran clean through the whole 02-06 window; three hours only, then up, so I can get a real night tonight.
The realignment sleep — this is the one that puts me back on Madrid nights after the Boston red-eye.
Day off, ordinary night, banking sleep before three standby days.
Standby tomorrow opens at 11:00Z, so a normal night and I'm callable rested.
Last normal night before the 13SEP early — get it while it's easy.
Afternoon nap on my day off purely to bank sleep for the 03:05Z report — I will not get a full night tonight and I know it.
Lights out at 20:00 local, which is unnatural, but with the alarm at 01:00Z and a 95-minute drive it's the only way to get seven hours before a four-sector day.
Home after eleven and a half hours and four landings on almost no sleep — short nap, then hold out for bedtime.
Nine hours to pay back the early; two days off after this so I can let it run long.
Ordinary night at home, staying anchored to Madrid time.
Full night before Dubai — a civilised 09:20Z report means no sleep debt going out.
23:30 to 07:30 Dubai time, which is also 21:30 to 05:30 on my body clock — a rare layover where local night and body night line up, so I take all of it.
Afternoon nap before the 13:10Z report; I'll be awake eighteen hours by the time I'm off duty in Madrid tonight.
In the door at 23:35Z off the Dubai sector; standby isn't until midday so I sleep straight through the morning.
Nap on the sofa mid-standby — tomorrow is a 05:00Z report and tonight's sleep will be short.
Straight to bed the moment standby releases, alarm at 02:45Z for a 03:25Z departure from home.
Two hours after the Dublin turnaround to clear the early-start debt before the worst night of the month.
Six hours only, on purpose — I need enough sleep pressure left to actually fall asleep in tomorrow's afternoon before the night duty.
The big one: seven hours in a dark room in the afternoon, because from 21:00Z I'm awake for eighteen hours straight across a four-sector night.
Home at 14:20Z off the all-nighter with another night duty possibly reporting at 18:30Z — two hours is all I can safely take, and it is not enough.
Off the second night duty and into bed; seven hours in the morning, then up so I don't wreck tonight.
Nine hours to put the body clock back on Madrid nights after two nights on the back of it.
Slightly short night on purpose so the pre-Singapore nap will take.
Two hours before leaving home at 11:10Z — the Singapore sector is 15h20 of duty finishing at 06:05 body time.
At the hotel by 12:35 Singapore time after a fifteen-hour duty — sleep immediately, seven hours, don't fight it.
04:00 to 12:00 Singapore local, which is 22:00 to 06:00 at home — I'm staying on Madrid time because the flight back reports at 15:50 body time.
Last top-up before the 13:50Z report; this duty finishes at 07:10 body time and crosses my whole window of low alertness.
In the door at 06:45Z off Singapore; a short morning sleep only, so I can still sleep tonight and be ready for Boston tomorrow.
The proper recovery night after the Singapore pairing, finished in time to leave home at 07:45Z.
17:30 to 01:30 Boston time looks odd but it is 23:30 to 07:30 at home — only one layover night, so I keep the Madrid clock rather than shift for it.
Eight hours on a half-shifted clock before the last duty; awake at 02:30 Boston local, but that's 08:30 body time and report is 12:55Z.
Blocks in at 23:45 local and home at 01:50 — the roster's last commute is the tiring bit, so nothing planned the next morning.

conflicts.statement: 21SEP is printed twice with two different four-sector night duties that overlap each other: one reporting 18:30Z and finishing 22SEP 03:53Z, the other reporting 22:45Z and finishing 22SEP 08:30Z. Both cannot be flown. Whichever is correct, it follows a 14h10 all-night duty that only ends at 21SEP 12:45Z, giving 5h45 or 10h00 rest between two consecutive back-of-the-clock duties.
options: Get crewing to confirm which of the two 21SEP lines stands before you plan anything else — this is the single biggest unknown in the month
If only the 22:45Z duty is real, extend the 21SEP recovery sleep from 14:45Z all the way to 21:00Z instead of stopping at 16:45Z
If the 18:30Z duty is real, you have a 2-hour nap between two night duties and I would raise a fatigue report rather than accept it
Ask whether the second line was meant to read 22SEP, which would make the sequence workable at roughly 10 hours' rest

conflicts.statement: Report is 03:05Z, which is 05:05 Madrid local. With a 95-minute commute you leave the door at 01:30Z and wake at 01:00Z, so the pre-duty sleep has to end at an hour when sleep is deepest. It is then a four-sector, 11h24 duty with the first two sectors flown entirely inside the 02:00-06:00 body-clock window.
options: Take the 12SEP afternoon nap as planned — it is not optional, it is most of the sleep you will get for this duty
Consider a hotel or crash pad near MAD on the night of 12SEP to convert 95 minutes of commute into 95 minutes of sleep
Expect the low point around the BCN-MAD and MAD-LHR sectors and plan controlled rest and caffeine accordingly
Flag to the operator that a 03:05Z report with a 95-minute commute is effectively a 01:00Z wake-up

conflicts.statement: Arrive BOS 07SEP 15:45Z and report back at 08:08 01:50Z — under 10 hours at the hotel, of which maybe 6h30 is sleepable, and it lands in the Boston afternoon. The duty then runs 01:50Z to 11:10Z, covering the entire 02:00-06:00 body-clock window with no local-night sleep beforehand.
options: Sleep on arrival at 17:15Z rather than trying to stay up — at 19:15 body time you will fall asleep, at 23:00 body time you will not
Blackout mask and earplugs; the Boston afternoon is the enemy here
Split rest with the other pilot in the cruise if the operator's scheme allows it
If the hotel transfer or room is not ready on arrival, say so at the time — the sleep opportunity is already marginal

conflicts.statement: 20SEP is a 14h10 duty reporting 22:35Z and finishing 21SEP 12:45Z, four sectors, all of it through the night and the whole low-alertness window. It follows a 05:00Z report on 19SEP, so the body clock is pulled early then pushed straight onto nights, and it is immediately followed by the disputed 21SEP night duty.
options: Protect the 20SEP afternoon sleep 12:30-19:30Z absolutely — no errands, no daylight, phone off
Deliberately trim the 19/20SEP night to six hours so the afternoon sleep will actually come
Raise a fatigue report for the 19SEP-to-21SEP sequence regardless of how the 21SEP duplicate resolves
Ask whether the DUB sectors on the back end of the 20SEP duty can be reallocated

conflicts.statement: 02SEP is marked DO but the previous duty does not end until 06:35Z that morning, and it ends in Bogota, not at base. The same pattern appears on 04SEP (duty ends 10:15Z), 22SEP (duty ends 03:53Z or 08:30Z), 25SEP (in SIN) and 27SEP (duty ends 05:10Z).
options: Treat these as post-duty rest days, not free days — do not plan anything on the morning of a DO that follows a night arrival
Confirm with crewing which of these count towards the ten days off credited on the roster header
Note that 25SEP as a 'day off' is a downroute day in Singapore on the wrong side of the clock

conflicts.statement: The 05SEP standby window is not printed directly; back-calculated from the 14:00Z end and 10h00 length it starts at 04:00Z, which is 06:00 Madrid local. It comes the day after a 12h05 overnight arrival from Bogota that only cleared at 10:15Z on 04SEP.
options: Confirm the standby start time with crewing — the roster only prints the end time and the length
Bed at 20:00Z on 04SEP so you have seven hours before the window opens
If called out early on 05SEP, be honest about how much sleep you actually got since the BOG arrival

conflicts.statement: The SIN pairing is two 15h20 duties. Outbound finishes 25SEP 04:05Z, which is 06:05 body time, and the return reports 26SEP 13:50Z and finishes 27SEP 05:10Z, again finishing right at the bottom of the body clock. The 34-hour Singapore layover is not long enough to adapt to a six-hour shift and should not be used to try.
options: Stay on Madrid time in Singapore as planned — sleep 04:00-12:00 SIN local, be awake through the SIN afternoon
Use the 26SEP 10:00Z nap before report; it is worth more than an extra hour in the morning
Plan in-flight rest to fall in the 02:00-06:00 body-time band on both sectors
Keep 27SEP genuinely clear — the morning sleep after this pairing is short and the real recovery is the following night

conflicts.statement: The roster gives two reporting offsets but does not label which flights are short or long haul. I applied 80 minutes to BOG, BOS, DXB and SIN and 50 minutes to BCN, LHR, DUB, FCO, LIS and CDG; every duty length printed on the roster reconciles exactly with those assumptions, including the 8h50 DXB duties.
options: Sanity-check the DXB report time of 13:10Z against your ops manual, since 7h00 block is a borderline long-haul call
If any offset differs, the affected pre-duty sleep block should move with it, not the wake-up time
